_note: Skeleton for docs/ledger-commit-exemptions.json — the factory data file read by tests/test_ledger_commit_cites_no_rows.py. Copy it into docs/ (the example itself is never read) and add an entry ONLY when a violation has an EMPTY REPAIR SPACE: the commit is pushed and cannot be amended, a revert cannot clear a gate that reads subjects across the marker range, and re-anchoring the marker past the violation would make the marker's own definition false and silently convert a live violation into an excused one. Key every entry by the FULL 40-character sha copied from live git output — a short sha or a tag matches nothing while looking like it should. The entry must PROVE the empty repair space and state the reason. It is printed as an 'excused:' line on EVERY gate run, so it is a visible debt rather than forgiveness, and the closing line distinguishes clean from excused. A malformed entry, or one that matches no violation, is a gate ERROR rather than a silent pass. A second entry of the same shape is a process defect, not an exemption: one is a debt, two mean the mechanism — running tools/audit.py before a commit that touches the ledger — is not biting.
